**Addition of water:** Ethanal is produced when $20\%$ sulfuric acid and $2\%$ mercuric sulphate are added to Ethyne at $80^{\circ}\text{C}$ temperature.

$$\text{CH}\equiv\text{CH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow[80^{\circ}\text{C}]{20\% \text{ H}_2\text{SO}_4, 2\% \text{ HgSO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$$
Ethyne $\quad\quad$ Water $\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad$ Ethanal

The bio-compounds which have hydroxyl radicals (-\text{OH}) are called Alcohols. However, some compounds are not called Alcohol though they have hydroxyl radicals (-\text{OH}). Such as- Phenol (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{OH}). General formula of alcohol is $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+1}\text{OH}$. The first member of this class is Methanol (\text{CH}_3-\text{OH}), second member is Ethanol (\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}). Alcohols can be symbolized by \text{R}-\text{OH}, where \text{R} is the alkyl radical. The initial members of this class are colour-less liquid substances and mix with water in all proportions.

**Naming:** Alcohols are named by omitting 'e' and adding (ol) with the names of Alkanes. Example: Ethanol (\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}).

**Preparation of Alcohol**

**From Ethyl Bromide:** Ethanol and sodium bromide are produced when liquid solution of sodium hydroxide is added with bromo ethane and heated.

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{NaOH} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{NaBr}$$
Bromo Ethane $\quad$ Sodium Hydroxide $\quad\quad\quad$ Ethanol $\quad\quad$ Sodium Bromide

The bio-compounds which have aldehyde group (-\text{CHO}) are called aldehyde.

**Naming:** Aldehydes are named by omitting 'e' and adding (al) with the names of alkanes. For example, propanal (\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}). The name of the first member of this class is methanal (\text{H}-\text{CHO}).
